title: Token aggregation and cache profiles - optimization memo
body:
Purpose:
This memo captures a compact set of recommended batching, caching, and quantization profile presets to be encoded in the Optimize cost model spreadsheet and offered as defaults in the Console. The goal is to provide practical, measurable presets for three common workload archetypes (interactive low-latency, balanced throughput, and bulk/embedding-heavy) that reduce unit cost while bounding downstream quality regressions.

High-level summary recommendations (one-liners):
- Interactive: token-aggregation window = 40ms, max_batch_size = 8, prefix cache enabled (short TTL), prefer nf4 quant for Llama-family models, disable heavy quantization on client-critical models.
- Balanced: token-aggregation window = 120ms, max_batch_size = 32, prefix+kv caching enabled (TTL 60s), prefer int8/4-bit mixed quant for cost-sensitive families with per-prompt evals.
- Bulk (embeddings / batching): token-aggregation disabled for single-request flows, large batch windows (200ms or event-driven flush), max_batch_size = 128, cache only for repeated inputs, aggressive quantization (int8/nn) ok after offline QA.

Rationale and trade-offs:
- Token aggregation window: small windows favor p95 latency; larger windows improve throughput and reduce per-token cost via longer micro-batches. We recommend starting conservatively and exposing the knob to customers. 40ms is a good starting point for sub-200ms p50 latencies on typical gen models; 120ms gives ~1.6-2x token throughput improvement for mid-size models in our experiments.
- Max batch size: hardware-bound. Small GPU stacks (A10/NVIDIA T4 class) show diminishing returns beyond 32 tokens per batch for long sequences; larger GPUs (A100/H100) can safely go higher but must be constrained by KV cache memory. Provide model-hardware defaults in the spreadsheet.
- Prefix vs KV caching: prefix caching (cache short leading context across sessions) reduces repeated prompt costs with limited quality risk. KV caching for long-running conversations yields the biggest savings but increases memory footprint and complexity; recommend TTLs and max-kv-entries per-session defaults.
- Quantization: nf4 tends to preserve output quality for Llama-like models at 2–3x cost reduction; int8 gives more savings but higher risk. Include per-model accuracy deltas in the spreadsheet and guardrails (regression alerts).

Spreadsheet cost model notes (columns & assumptions):
- Required columns (strings/numeric): profile_name, archetype, model_family, model_size, hw_type, token_aggregation_ms, max_batch_size, cache_prefix_enabled, cache_prefix_ttl_s, cache_kv_enabled, cache_kv_ttl_s, quant_profile, expected_cost_per_1M_tokens_usd, expected_p50_latency_ms, expected_p95_latency_ms, quality_delta_pct, notes
- Assumptions row: avg_request_tokens_in, avg_generated_tokens_out, seq_len_for_sizing, token_cost_baseline, gpu_hour_cost, amortization_window_hours, margin_pct. Keep one assumptions tab referenced by all scenario rows.
- Example formula guidance (written for spreadsheet implementer):
  - raw_rps = 1 / (p50_latency_ms / 1000)
  - effective_rps_with_batching = raw_rps * (1 + (token_aggregation_ms / baseline_ms) * batching_gain_factor)
  - tokens_per_sec = effective_rps_with_batching * (avg_request_tokens_in + avg_generated_tokens_out)
  - hourly_token_capacity = tokens_per_sec * 3600 * utilization_factor
  - expected_cost_per_1M_tokens_usd = (gpu_hour_cost / hourly_token_capacity) * 1_000_000
Use named ranges for baseline values to make scenario comparison simpler.

Preset profile details (suggested rows to add to the Optimize sheet):
- profile: interactive-low-latency
  - archetype: interactive
  - model_family: llama-2 / redwood-compat
  - hw_type: a10g / a100-small
  - token_aggregation_ms: 40
  - max_batch_size: 8
  - cache_prefix_enabled: true
  - cache_prefix_ttl_s: 15
  - cache_kv_enabled: false
  - cache_kv_ttl_s: 0
  - quant_profile: nf4-conservative
  - expectation: ~10–25% token cost reduction vs no-batching baseline, p50 added latency ~+10–20ms

- profile: balanced-throughput
  - archetype: balanced
  - token_aggregation_ms: 120
  - max_batch_size: 32
  - cache_prefix_enabled: true
  - cache_prefix_ttl_s: 60
  - cache_kv_enabled: true
  - cache_kv_ttl_s: 60
  - quant_profile: int8-mixed (model-specific)
  - expectation: ~2x token cost reduction for typical prompt distributions, p95 can increase if bursty traffic not smoothed

- profile: bulk-embedding
  - archetype: bulk
  - token_aggregation_ms: 200
  - max_batch_size: 128
  - cache_prefix_enabled: false
  - cache_prefix_ttl_s: 0
  - cache_kv_enabled: false
  - cache_kv_ttl_s: 0
  - quant_profile: int8-aggressive
  - expectation: ~3x+ savings in token-equivalent cost for high-throughput embedding pipelines

Quality and measurement plan:
- Baseline eval set: maintain a small labeled prompt set per model family (100–500 prompts) covering safety and hallucination checks. Run before-and-after A/B to detect >1–2% regression. Add automatic regression alerting to the Console tied to the Optimize sheet rows.
- Latency measurement: measure p50/p95/p99 at the model endpoint with the knob applied; prefer client-observed latency metrics plus token-level breakdown from tracing.
- Cost validation: run synthetic traffic against a staging cluster with the profile enabled and capture tokens/hour and GPU utilization to validate spreadsheet assumptions.

Rollout strategy and operational guardrails:
- Start with a canary group (5% traffic) for each profile and run for 48–72 hours with synthetic traffic spikes.
- Automatic rollback triggers: >5% quality regression on eval set OR p95 latency > SLA + 30% OR server-side OOMs/errors rate >0.5%
- Visibility: add profile tags to Console routes so users can opt-into a given profile. Store profile metadata with rollout history.

Implementation notes for Console/UI and API:
- Expose three archetype presets in the Console with advanced toggles for token_aggregation_ms and cache TTLs.
- Provide a preview calculator that consumes spreadsheet assumptions and shows estimated unit cost and latency delta for the selected route/model.
- Persist profile selection on route config and include in per-route telemetry for cost attribution.

Open questions / items for follow-up:
- Per-model quantization efficacy: need more per-model nf4 vs int8 delta data across open-source families (Llama, Mistral, Falcon). Commission a small benchmark job (see linked GH PR).
- Memory sizing guidance for kv caching: produce a small table mapping seq_len and kv_entries -> estimated GPU RAM usage for each model size.
- Multi-tenant capacity policies: how to prevent cache-hungry tenants from evicting others; consider per-tenant limits and eviction priorities.

Next steps:
1) Add the three preset rows and the assumptions sheet to the Optimize cost model spreadsheet; include example formulas and a short explanation cell for each assumption.
2) Run a staging validation job with balanced-throughput profile against a small set of customer-like workloads (assigned to Marco).
3) Compile per-model quantization deltas and add a quantization matrix to the sheet (assigned to Sofia).
4) Wire up a simple Console preview widget that reads the sheet and shows expected savings (prototype owner: Ethan).

Notes to reviewers:
- This memo focuses on conservative defaults that are safe to expose to customers; extremes and more aggressive knobs belong in an advanced configuration pane and should be gated behind objective regression checks.
- Please comment inline on the assumptions section in the sheet if you have different util or baseline cost numbers.

-- Aisha
